en.title: Universal wisdom for you and your Agent: 12 foundational common-sense principles and execution rules for knowledge workers (with open-source Skill uw-mode)
en.summary: Keep reminding AI to "think it through before acting and check before delivering," yet it still goes off the rails? The author rewrote 12 everyday working principles—begin with the end in mind, the 80/20 rule, reverse thinking—into concrete rules an Agent can execute: when to ask follow-up questions, when to stop and recheck, and what must be verified before delivery. It might just help!

en.title: AI blueprint for finance teams
en.summary:
An AI Blueprint for Finance Teams

Finance leaders have a clear mandate: prove ROI on AI, govern AI costs, and reshape how the CFO's office operates. In this keynote, Snowflake CFO Brian Robins will share the trends, challenges and opportunities finance teams face today, and explain how Snowflake's own finance team uses Snowflake. The session then follows a CFO through the full continuous close cycle — from accelerating the close and analyzing variances to reforecasting and preparing for earnings — all powered by trusted data and AI. Finally, a customer will share how a leading company is reimagining AI-driven finance management in practice.
en.reason: Snowflake CFO Brian Robins will outline how finance teams prove AI ROI and govern AI costs, then show Snowflake’s own finance team using trusted data and AI across continuous close, variance analysis, reforecasting and earnings preparation.

These 10 projects are not substitutes for one another; they sit at different points along the video production pipeline:

en.title: codex with a local model caps single-output at 3,208 tokens: a complete, follow-along tutorial you can actually fix it with
en.summary:
When codex is pointed at a local model, output stalls at 3208 tokens. Supplying metadata through model_catalog_json and setting truncation_policy.limit to 16384 keeps long outputs from being cut off.

I connected codex to a Qwen3.8 model running on local Strata (RTX 5060 Ti 16GB + 64GB RAM, 131072 context, served at 127.0.0.1:8080).

Everyday Q&A is fine, and so are small file edits. But when I asked it to edit a 200-plus-line script, it stopped halfway and left two lines on screen:

The context is clearly 131072, yet a single output only gets 3208 — 2.4%.

This tutorial walks through the full process of raising output length to 16384. Just follow along: first figure out which case you're in, then apply the change with a one-click script, and finally verify against three criteria. If the script doesn't work, there's a manual path and an error lookup table further down.

Check the three cases below — only the third requires a config change:

The test is one line: whether codex prints this on startup.

If it does, codex doesn't recognize your model and is falling back to default metadata — that's where 3208 comes from.

Before changing the config, confirm you actually need to.

Option A: break the task down. Have it write one file at a time, no more than 200 lines per pass.
en.reason: Codex with a local Qwen3.8 model on an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB stalled at 3208 output tokens, 2.4% of its 131072 context; the fix sets truncation_policy.limit to 16384 via model_catalog_json, plus a one-shot script, manual path and error table.

从救火队长，到当到老板，把 Router-Worker 架构融入到我的 AI Native 工作台。
哈喽，我是 lv。
最近 DeepSeek Harness 团队发布的一篇关于 Super Agent 架构的文章。
文章里提出的一个观点，直接戳中了我每天使用 AI Coding 工作台时的痛点：
多任务执行的上限，受限于人的注意力的上限。
放到我自己身上，我最多同时并行 3 个 session window。超过 3 个，注意力就散了，效率反而会降低。
注意，这里我说的还是 session，比如一个 Claude Code 的对话。本质上，它并不等于一个任务。
因为对一个任务来说，「进行中」和「已完成」不应该跟着 session 的生命周期走：
这就会带来一个问题：我人在不同的 session 之间切换，当并发量上来、再加上优先级插队，就很容易出现任务被遗忘。
比如，我当前并行了 A、B、C 三个 session。session A 给我发了通知，我正准备处理。
这时来了一个紧急 bug，我开了一个新的 session D 去处理。session A 的通知我已经点开过了，但还没来

en.title: After a week of grinding, I integrated the Super Agent architecture into my AI-native workbench
en.summary:
From firefighter to boss: folding the Router-Worker architecture into my AI Native workbench

Hi, I'm lv.

Recently the DeepSeek Harness team published an article on the Super Agent architecture. One idea in it landed squarely on a pain point I hit every day when using an AI Coding workbench:

The ceiling on multitasking is set by the ceiling on human attention.

In my own case, I can run at most 3 session windows in parallel. Beyond 3, my attention scatters and efficiency actually drops. Note that I'm talking about sessions here — a Claude Code conversation, say. A session isn't the same thing as a task. For a task, "in progress" and "completed" shouldn't follow a session's lifecycle.

That creates a problem: as I switch between sessions, once concurrency climbs and higher-priority items cut in, tasks easily get forgotten. Say I'm running three sessions in parallel, A, B, and C. Session A pings me and I'm about to deal with it. Then an urgent bug comes in, so I open a new session D to handle it. I've already clicked open session A's notification, but haven't gotten to it yet
en.reason: lv folds the Super Agent Router-Worker architecture into an AI Native workbench, addressing the max-3-session attention limit with a 7-state task kanban and a four-window example that derives states from session facts.

en.summary:
An AI Blueprint for Finance Teams

Finance leaders have a clear mandate: prove ROI on AI, govern AI costs, and reshape how the CFO's office operates. In this keynote, Snowflake CFO Brian Robins will share the trends, challenges and opportunities finance teams face today, and explain how Snowflake's own finance team uses Snowflake. The session then follows a CFO through the full continuous close cycle — from accelerating the close and analyzing variances to reforecasting and preparing for earnings — all powered by trusted data and AI. Finally, a customer will share how a leading company is reimagining AI-driven finance management in practice.
en.reason: Snowflake CFO Brian Robins will outline how finance teams prove AI ROI and govern AI costs, then show Snowflake’s own finance team using trusted data and AI across continuous close, variance analysis, reforecasting and earnings preparation.

At the same time, programmatic video approaches built with React/Python are eating into some use cases of traditional editing software.

This article does three things:

First, the methodology: Stars measure popularity, not quality. Half the projects on the list are new repos created only in 2026, growing very fast. Whether they are worth betting on still depends on Issue response speed and Release cadence; each will be noted below.

These 10 projects are not substitutes for one another; they sit at different points along the video production pipeline:

This is the most crowded and fastest-growing camp on the 2026 list, taking 6 of the 10 slots. Their common traits: LLMs write scripts, models generate assets, TTS handles voiceover, and FFmpeg handles final compositing and export.

en.title: codex with a local model caps single-output at 3,208 tokens: a complete, follow-along tutorial you can actually fix it with
en.summary:
When codex is pointed at a local model, output stalls at 3208 tokens. Supplying metadata through model_catalog_json and setting truncation_policy.limit to 16384 keeps long outputs from being cut off.

I connected codex to a Qwen3.8 model running on local Strata (RTX 5060 Ti 16GB + 64GB RAM, 131072 context, served at 127.0.0.1:8080).

Everyday Q&A is fine, and so are small file edits. But when I asked it to edit a 200-plus-line script, it stopped halfway and left two lines on screen:

The context is clearly 131072, yet a single output only gets 3208 — 2.4%.

This tutorial walks through the full process of raising output length to 16384. Just follow along: first figure out which case you're in, then apply the change with a one-click script, and finally verify against three criteria. If the script doesn't work, there's a manual path and an error lookup table further down.

Check the three cases below — only the third requires a config change:

The test is one line: whether codex prints this on startup.

If it does, codex doesn't recognize your model and is falling back to default metadata — that's where 3208 comes from.

Before changing the config, confirm you actually need to.

Option A: break the task down. Have it write one file at a time, no more than 200 lines per pass.
en.reason: Codex with a local Qwen3.8 model on an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB stalled at 3208 output tokens, 2.4% of its 131072 context; the fix sets truncation_policy.limit to 16384 via model_catalog_json, plus a one-shot script, manual path and error table.

en.title: After a week of grinding, I integrated the Super Agent architecture into my AI-native workbench
en.summary:
From firefighter to boss: folding the Router-Worker architecture into my AI Native workbench

Hi, I'm lv.

Recently the DeepSeek Harness team published an article on the Super Agent architecture. One idea in it landed squarely on a pain point I hit every day when using an AI Coding workbench:

The ceiling on multitasking is set by the ceiling on human attention.

In my own case, I can run at most 3 session windows in parallel. Beyond 3, my attention scatters and efficiency actually drops. Note that I'm talking about sessions here — a Claude Code conversation, say. A session isn't the same thing as a task. For a task, "in progress" and "completed" shouldn't follow a session's lifecycle.

That creates a problem: as I switch between sessions, once concurrency climbs and higher-priority items cut in, tasks easily get forgotten. Say I'm running three sessions in parallel, A, B, and C. Session A pings me and I'm about to deal with it. Then an urgent bug comes in, so I open a new session D to handle it. I've already clicked open session A's notification, but haven't gotten to it yet
en.reason: lv folds the Super Agent Router-Worker architecture into an AI Native workbench, addressing the max-3-session attention limit with a 7-state task kanban and a four-window example that derives states from session facts.
